correctness.rationale: Analytical proof: no boundary max by f prime at zero; equal-stationarity plus Hessian sign forces at most one large mean; strictly increasing t coth t solves n=2; nonnegative convex envelope g_n of log moment-generating ratios yields exactly one switch for n>=3; cubic perturbation and strict concavity give location and jump; stationarity gives asymptotics. All budget and dimension ranges and equality cases handled. Supplementary checker passed 62645 numerical assertions; not used for infinitary claims.

value.rationale: Seed-predator brood pollination provides a concrete reason repeated visits can harm viability. This exact single-visit response has a structurally unexpected n=2 versus n>=3 change from continuous to discontinuous allocation optima. The n-dependent rigorous phase boundary informs when equal flower visitation fails in a fixed-traffic model. The precise result is neither an arbitrary slice nor merely a trivial Poisson probability; its ecological and controllability limitations are explicitly stated.
